description: Migrated to Spring Cloud Azure approach for PostgreSQL Managed Identity authentication. Added spring-cloud-azure-dependencies BOM (version 4.20.0) for centralized dependency management, compatible with Spring Boot 2.x. Replaced com.azure:azure-identity-extensions with spring-cloud-azure-starter-jdbc-postgresql which provides a cleaner, more idiomatic integration for Spring Boot applications. This approach improves code maintainability by using Spring Cloud Azure configuration properties instead of embedded JDBC URL parameters.

Migrated PostgreSQL datasource configuration from JDBC URL-based authentication (using azure-identity-extensions plugin) to Spring Cloud Azure property-based configuration for passwordless authentication. Updated environment variable names from PGHOST/PGPORT/PGDATABASE to POSTGRESQL_SERVER/POSTGRESQL_PORT/POSTGRESQL_DATABASE following Azure naming conventions. Changed datasource URL format to Azure PostgreSQL format: jdbc:postgresql://${POSTGRESQL_SERVER}.postgresql.database.azure.com:${POSTGRESQL_PORT}/${POSTGRESQL_DATABASE}?sslMode=REQUIRED. Removed hardcoded password by enabling spring.datasource.azure.passwordless-enabled=true for automatic access token retrieval. Added managed identity configuration: spring.cloud.azure.credential.client-id and spring.cloud.azure.credential.managed-identity-enabled=true. Added comprehensive documentation for service principal and Azure sovereign cloud authentication. Functional equivalence maintained: both JDBC plugin and Spring Cloud Azure approaches use Managed Identity for authentication, with identical security and reliability properties.

Applied identical Managed Identity datasource migration as main application.properties to Docker configuration profile. Updated from JDBC URL plugin-based authentication to Spring Cloud Azure property-based configuration. Changed environment variables to POSTGRESQL_SERVER/POSTGRESQL_PORT/POSTGRESQL_DATABASE for consistency. Updated datasource URL to Azure PostgreSQL format with sslMode=REQUIRED. Added spring.datasource.azure.passwordless-enabled=true and managed identity credential configuration (client-id, managed-identity-enabled). Ensures consistent passwordless authentication behavior between standard and containerized deployments.
Administrative metadata update to record task completion status and success criteria validation. Changes are administrative and do not affect application functionality or behavior.
